hints: Notice the shapes in the top diagram: $X$ is long and points up-left while $Y$ is shorter and points directly right.
Rearrange $X = Y - Z$ to make $Z$ the subject to get $Z = Y - X$, so you need $Y$ plus the reverse of $X$.
Reverse $X$ to point down-right, then add the small rightward $Y$ to it - which way and roughly how long is the resultant?
walkthrough: Start from the given equation $X = Y - Z$ and rearrange for $Z$ by adding $Z$ to both sides and subtracting $X$, giving $Z = Y - X$.
Recall vector subtraction means adding the negative vector, so $Z = Y + (-X)$ where $-X$ has the same length as $X$ but opposite direction.
$X$ points up and to the left, so $-X$ points down and to the right with the same long length.
Add the vector $Y$, which is a short arrow to the right, to the tail or tip of $-X$ using tip-to-tail addition.
The resultant must still point down and to the right and remain long, because the long down-right $-X$ dominates the short rightward $Y$.

options.A: Points down and to the right with length matching $Y-X$, which is $Y$ plus the long down-right reversed $X$.
options.B: Points up and to the left, which is the direction of $X$ itself rather than $Y-X$.
options.C: Points straight up and is too short, ignoring the rightward $Y$ and the rightward component from subtracting $X$.
options.D: Points straight down and is too short, ignoring the horizontal components of $X$ and $Y$.
